title: The Drowned Town
logline: A dry year drops the water behind a dam far enough for the streets of a town drowned decades ago to come back into the air, and the people who grew up there walk out across the mud looking for houses that are no longer where they remember.
human_question: When the map we carry no longer matches the ground, how do we find our way?

situation.what_happens: A settlement was flooded when a reservoir was built, and its people were resettled a generation or more ago. In a severe dry year the water falls far enough to expose foundations, steps, wells and thresholds, and word travels among the former residents that the town is briefly back. They walk out across the cracked bed and try to match what they remember against what is in front of them, often disagreeing about which ruin was whose. Then the rain comes and the water closes over it again.
situation.who_is_involved: Former residents and their grown children, who are the only people able to read the ground; younger family members who have only ever heard about the place; and, at a distance, the authority that manages the water and the access.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the former residents, a memory either confirmed or quietly lost, and a loss long since settled being reopened for a few weeks. For their children, a story either becoming a place or staying a story. For the film, the danger of turning other people's displacement into a spectacle.
situation.how_it_unfolds: It begins with a rumour and a water level, moves through days of walking, pacing out streets and arguing gently, and is ended by the weather rather than by anyone's decision. Some people find what they came for, some find that they cannot, and some choose not to come at all. Reality decides whether there is a drawdown, how much it exposes, and when it goes under again.

concept_merge.why_together: C074 brings the compendium's account of what lies dormant: states that lie asleep in the mind-stream and rise again when a suitable object appears, so that not reacting today proves very little [C074-P:L474; C074-P:L486–L498; C074-M:L75]. C008 brings the everyday face of a mind that cannot take in what is in front of it [C008-P:L34]. The town under the water gives the first its image; the people standing on the foundations give the second its human weight.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That hiddenness is not absence, and that finding this out is disorienting rather than dramatic. C074 alone would be a diagram. C008 alone would be a mood. Together they show why what lies low is so easily mistaken for what is finished.

concept_links.why: The digest describes latent tendencies as lying asleep until something wakes them, and reports the sources' example of hermits far from temptation who still fall when the right object meets them [C074-P:L474; C074-P:L486–L498; C074-M:L75]. The drowned town is an image of what lies low until conditions change. It is not a picture of anyone's mind: the residents' memories and grief are not defilements, and the digest also rules out the reading that the mind is pure underneath.

The digest reads the two delusion-rooted minds as the everyday experience of being lost, stuck at a fork or running in circles, and describes doubt generally as a mind that cannot decide about its object [C008-P:L34]. People standing on a foundation unable to agree where they are carry that description. The link reaches no further: the sources' harmful doubt is restricted to eight religious matters, and a disagreement about a remembered street is not it.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Something you cannot see is not necessarily gone. The texts describe some states of mind as lying hidden, like a town under water, and rising again when conditions change.
what_must_be_real: The drought, the drawdown and the returning residents. No one is brought to the site for the camera, no memory is scripted, no grief is asked for, and the resettlement history is not flattened into a story with a villain.
position_hint: middle, sitting early in the group: it follows the opening by moving from not knowing the way to not being able to trust what one already knows, and it makes the group's plainest statement that what is covered has not gone.
risks: Grief and displacement filmed as spectacle; the resettlement history is painful and may be politically sensitive.
Presenting the residents' memory, or their disagreement, as confusion or as a defilement.
The image doing the work that the people should do.
Exposed reservoir ground may not be safe to stand on.
drop_if: No drawdown exposes the remains during the development window.
Former residents do not wish to return with a camera.

connections.note: A place that has lost its bearings, and a traveller who has.
The group opens on something covered by water and closes on something covered by cloud.

selection.reason: Carries the group's second episode and is the only idea that shows a thing lying hidden and returning when conditions change.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
Whether any submerged settlement has re-emerged recently, and when it might again, is unconfirmed.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
